senses.definition: (countable) A country's entire maritime military force, including ships and personnel.
examples: People who get seasick easily shouldn't join the navy.

quotes.text: The skipper Mr. Cooke had hired at Far Harbor was a God-fearing man with a luke warm interest in his new billet and employer, and had only been prevailed upon to take charge of the yacht after the offer of an emolument equal to half a year's sea pay of an ensign in the navy.
quotes.reference: 1897 December (indicated as 1898), Winston Churchill, chapter X, in The Celebrity: An Episode, New York, N.Y.: The Macmillan Company; London: Macmillan & Co., Ltd., →OCLC:

senses.definition: (countable) A governmental department in charge of a country's maritime military force.
(archaic, countable) Any fleet of maritime vessels, and especially the entire fleet of any particular nationality, including vessels that are commercial, military, or both.
(countable and uncountable) A dark blue colour, usually called navy blue.
Having the dark blue colour of navy blue.

quotes.text: The cover is as navy as a bruise.
